proficiencyLevels.name: Novice
proficiencyLevels.description: Just learning the skill; requires close supervision.

proficiencyLevels.name: Practitioner
proficiencyLevels.description: Can apply the skill on routine work with occasional guidance.
genericBehaviors: Recognizes when to ask for help.

proficiencyLevels.name: Proficient
proficiencyLevels.description: Applies the skill confidently across most work; the team baseline.

proficiencyLevels.name: Advanced
proficiencyLevels.description: Sets standards; coaches others; handles ambiguous problems.

proficiencyLevels.name: Expert
proficiencyLevels.description: Recognized authority; influences industry or company-wide direction.
genericBehaviors: Recognized externally as a subject-matter authority.

levelDescriptions.1: Familiar with syntax; can read TypeScript code.
levelDescriptions.2: Writes simple TypeScript with basic types and interfaces.
levelDescriptions.3: Comfortable with generics, mapped types, and conditional types.
levelDescriptions.4: Designs type-safe APIs and tooling; reviews complex type code.
levelDescriptions.5: Contributes to TypeScript ecosystem (libraries, type definitions, RFCs).

1: Reads TypeScript files in code review with help.
2: Adds type annotations to existing JavaScript modules.
3: Refactors a module to use discriminated unions.
4: Designs a generic type-safe API client used across teams.
5: Authors a TypeScript ESLint rule used company-wide.

levelDescriptions.1: Reads system design docs; understands diagrams.
levelDescriptions.3: Designs multi-component systems within a team scope.
levelDescriptions.4: Designs cross-team systems considering reliability, scale, and cost.
levelDescriptions.5: Defines architecture vision spanning the platform; mentors architects.

1: Reviews ADRs and asks clarifying questions.
2: Drafts a design doc for a new endpoint.
3: Owns the design for a service-level rewrite.
4: Leads cross-team architecture review for a quarterly initiative.
5: Defines the platform's three-year architecture roadmap.

levelDescriptions.1: Has not yet conducted a code review.
levelDescriptions.2: Reviews routine PRs; catches obvious issues.
levelDescriptions.3: Catches subtle issues; gives constructive feedback consistently.
levelDescriptions.4: Reviews complex PRs; teaches reviewers; sets review standards.
levelDescriptions.5: Designs the code-review program for the company.

2: Approves PRs after suggesting style improvements.
3: Identifies design and security issues before merge.
5: Defines company-wide review standards and tooling.

levelDescriptions.1: Reads Kubernetes manifests; understands Pod and Service concepts.
levelDescriptions.2: Deploys applications using Helm or kustomize with guidance.
levelDescriptions.3: Diagnoses production issues; configures HPA, PDB, and resource quotas.
levelDescriptions.4: Designs cluster topology; manages multi-cluster operations.
levelDescriptions.5: Contributes to Kubernetes upstream; defines org-wide cluster standards.

2: Deploys a feature service using the team's Helm chart.
3: Resolves a production OOMKilled incident; tunes resource limits.
4: Designs the multi-region cluster failover plan.
5: Authors a CNCF KEP for a feature adopted upstream.

levelDescriptions.1: Reads pipeline YAML; understands build steps.
levelDescriptions.2: Modifies pipeline scripts to add a step or job.
levelDescriptions.3: Designs end-to-end pipelines for a service; tunes performance.
levelDescriptions.4: Designs cross-team pipeline standards; manages pipeline platform.
levelDescriptions.5: Defines org-wide CI/CD architecture; mentors pipeline platform engineers.

2: Adds a new lint step to the team's pipeline.
3: Designs the deploy-on-merge pipeline for the platform service.
4: Owns the company's GitHub Actions composite-actions library.
5: Architects the company's monorepo build orchestration.

levelDescriptions.3: Facilitates productive discussions; manages competing priorities.
levelDescriptions.4: Influences senior leaders; aligns cross-functional groups.
levelDescriptions.5: Sets enterprise-level stakeholder strategy; coaches managers.

1: Lists project stakeholders in a kickoff doc.
2: Sends weekly status updates to the team.
3: Facilitates a roadmap review with conflicting team needs.
4: Aligns three VP-level stakeholders on a quarterly initiative.

levelDescriptions.1: Has not yet mentored another engineer.
levelDescriptions.2: Mentors a single junior engineer through one project cycle.
levelDescriptions.3: Mentors multiple engineers; gives consistent feedback.
levelDescriptions.4: Coaches other mentors; designs onboarding programs.
levelDescriptions.5: Sets mentoring strategy company-wide; coaches senior coaches.

1: Pairs with a peer during code review.
2: Onboards a new hire on the team.
3: Mentors three engineers across a year; gives quarterly feedback.
5: Speaks at industry events on engineering mentorship.

levelDescriptions.2: Coordinates with one other team for a feature.
levelDescriptions.3: Drives cross-team initiatives; resolves conflicts directly.
levelDescriptions.4: Leads cross-org programs; influences functional partners.
levelDescriptions.5: Defines the company's cross-functional engagement playbook.

1: Attends standup with a partner team.
2: Coordinates a feature spanning eng + design.
3: Drives a cross-team initiative across 4 squads.
4: Leads an enterprise program with eng, product, ops, and CX.
5: Defines how the company runs cross-functional initiatives.

levelDescriptions.1: Reads runbooks; understands the on-call process.
levelDescriptions.2: Handles routine alerts with runbook guidance.
levelDescriptions.3: Acts as primary on-call; runs incidents; writes RCAs.
levelDescriptions.4: Acts as Incident Commander; coaches IC trainees.

2: Resolves a P3 alert using the runbook.
3: Leads response to a P1 incident; writes the postmortem.
4: Trains new ICs; runs incident game days.
5: Authors the company's IR playbook and SEV taxonomy.

levelDescriptions.1: Reads domain models; recognizes bounded contexts.
levelDescriptions.2: Implements features within an existing domain model.
levelDescriptions.3: Designs domain models for a new bounded context.
levelDescriptions.4: Designs cross-domain integration; resolves model conflicts.

2: Implements a feature using the existing aggregate root.
3: Designs a new bounded context for a quarterly initiative.
4: Mediates a cross-domain conflict between two teams.
